title: Derived affine stalk and inverse-image base-skyscraper tensor comparisons
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings, $f:U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ its scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], and $M^\bullet$ an arbitrary complex of $A$-modules. Let $\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ be its termwise associated-sheaf complex [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Put $\mathcal B=f^{-1}\mathcal O_V$ and $C^\bullet=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}\widetilde{M^\bullet}$, where $\alpha:\mathcal B\to\mathcal O_U$ is the canonical structure map [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $x=\mathfrak q\in U$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Let $e_x:R_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal B_x$ be the composite of the affine germ isomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{V,f(x)}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] and the inverse-image structure stalk isomorphism $\mathcal O_{V,f(x)}\cong\mathcal B_x$ [lem-pc-inverse-image-structure-stalk-iso], and let $S_x$ be the module stalk functor at $x$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] followed by restriction of scalars along $e_x$, applied termwise to complexes. In the unbounded derived category $D(R_{\mathfrak p})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is an isomorphism $\theta_x:Q(S_x C^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q})$, where localization is termwise [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and the right side has scalars restricted along the induced map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$. For every K-flat resolution $u:P^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], $\theta_x\circ Q(S_x u):Q(S_x P^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q})$ is an isomorphism in $D(R_{\mathfrak p})$. No flatness, finiteness, boundedness or Noetherian assumption is imposed. Write $S_x$ also for the functor on derived categories induced by the exact stalk and scalar transport. For every $\mathcal O_V$-module sheaf $\mathcal G$, there is an isomorphism in $D(R_{\mathfrak p})$,
$$S_x(QC^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}f^{-1}\mathcal G)\cong Q(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q})\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}\mathcal G_{f(x)}.$$
The inverse-image module structure is the canonical one obtained by multiplying local representatives before sheafification [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module]; the stalk $\mathcal G_{f(x)}$ is viewed over $R_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{V,f(x)}$. For every $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$, let $\mathcal G=i_{f(x),*}L$ be the ringed-module skyscraper on $V$ [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper]. Then $\mathcal G_{f(x)}\cong L$ and $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x\cong L$, linearly under $e_x$, and the displayed comparison specializes to an isomorphism with right side $Q(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q})\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}L$. Sheaf derived tensors are defined by K-flat resolutions [def-trf-ringed-complex-derived-tensor-vanishing], and module derived tensors likewise use K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tag 0DHY, lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine, opening affine stalk identifications; derived stalk tensor comparison and inverse-image base-skyscraper realization expanding the cited stalk argument.

proof.text: Write $y=f(x)$, $T=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B=\mathcal B_x$. Let $k:\mathcal O_{V,y}\to B$ be the canonical inverse-image ring stalk comparison: the presheaf inverse-image stalk map, sending $s_y$ to the germ of the coprojection of $s$, followed by the stalk of the sheafification map. The first map is a ring isomorphism by the presheaf inverse-image stalk theorem for commutative rings, and the second is a bijective ring homomorphism by the sheafification stalk theorem; so $k$ is a ring isomorphism. On germs $\alpha_x(k(s_y))=(f^\sharp s)_x$, so $\alpha_x k=f^\sharp_x$: $k$ is the inverse-image structure stalk isomorphism of the statement, and it is the same $k$ as in the relative stalk restriction lemma and in the semilinear inverse-image comparison of Step 4. Let $j:T\cong\mathcal O_{V,y}$ be the affine germ isomorphism, so $e_x=kj$. The relative inverse-image stalk restriction lemma, applied to $K=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$, gives an isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O_{V,y}$-modules between the restriction along $k$ of the stalk complex at $x$ of $C^\bullet=\operatorname{Res}_\alpha\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ and the restriction along $f^\sharp_x$ of the stalk complex $\widetilde{M^\bullet}_x$; restricting further along $j$ gives $S_xC^\bullet\cong\operatorname{Res}_{f^\sharp_x j}\widetilde{M^\bullet}_x$ over $T$. The affine scheme stalk-map formula identifies $f^\sharp_x j$ with $r/s\mapsto f(r)/f(s)$ into $A_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{U,x}$, the scalar action on $M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}$ in the statement. In each degree the tilde-stalk localization theorem gives an $\mathcal O_{U,x}$-linear, hence $T$-linear, isomorphism $\widetilde{M^n}_x\cong M^n_{\mathfrak q}$ sending the germ of $\tau(m)$ to $m/1$, and so the germ of $a^{-1}\tau(m)$ to $m/a$ for $a\notin\mathfrak q$. It commutes with differentials: the differential of the termwise associated-sheaf complex is $\widetilde{d_M}$, with $\widetilde{d_M}\tau=\tau d_M$, so both composites send the germ of $a^{-1}\tau(m)$ to $d(m)/a$, and every stalk element is such a fraction. Composing gives an actual isomorphism of complexes $t:S_xC^\bullet\cong M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}$ with the prescribed base-local-ring action.

proof.text: The module-stalk exactness theorem applies to the ringed space $(U,\mathcal B)$, irrespective of its relation to $\mathcal O_U$. Restriction of scalars along $e_x$ is exact because kernels and cokernels have the same underlying additive groups and maps. Hence $S_x$ is exact. The exact-functor derived-factorization theorem therefore gives its functor on unbounded derived categories and the comparison $S_x(QK)\cong Q(S_xK)$. Put $\theta_x=Q(t)$. A K-flat resolution $u:P^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism by definition; exactness implies $S_xu$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The localization defining the derived category inverts it, so both $\theta_x$ and $\theta_x\circ Q(S_xu)$ are isomorphisms. K-flatness is not needed for this last assertion beyond the resolution hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; modules.tex Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian; perfect.tex Tag 0DHY, opening stalk identification.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $u:P^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ on the ringed site $(U,\mathcal B)$ using the ringed-site resolution theorem. The ringed-space K-flat stalk criterion implies that $P_x^\bullet$ is K-flat over $B$. Transport along the ring isomorphism $e_x:T\cong B$ makes $S_xP^\bullet$ K-flat over $T$: for any acyclic $T$-complex $N$, give its same groups the $B$-action through $e_x^{-1}$; it remains acyclic, and the balanced tensors $S_xP\otimes_T N$ and $P_x\otimes_B N$ are identified by $p\otimes n\mapsto p\otimes n$, with the same total differential. The latter is acyclic by K-flatness. This uses only a ring isomorphism, and does not assert that restriction along the possibly nonflat map $T\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ preserves K-flatness.

For an arbitrary $\mathcal O_V$-module $\mathcal G$, put $H=f^{-1}\mathcal G$, with the module structure obtained by multiplying representatives before sheafification. The semilinear inverse-image stalk comparison, whose ring map is the same canonical $k$ as in Step 1, gives $c_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G_y\cong H_x$ with $c_{\mathcal G}(r m)=k(r)c_{\mathcal G}(m)$. Let $j:T\cong\mathcal O_{V,y}$ be the affine germ isomorphism, so $e_x=kj$. Thus $\gamma_{\mathcal G}=c_{\mathcal G}^{-1}:S_xH\cong\mathcal G_y$ is $T$-linear: $c_{\mathcal G}(j(a)m)=e_x(a)c_{\mathcal G}(m)$. This verifies the actual inverse-image scalar action rather than replacing it with extension of scalars to $\mathcal O_{U,x}$.

source.place: Tag 008H, lemma-stalk-pullback; Tags 008X/008Y, inverse-image module action; Tag 0098, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules, proof.

proof.text: The ringed-site K-flat tensor comparison, applied to $P$ and $H$, and $Q(u):QP\cong QC$, represents $QC\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}H$ by $Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\mathcal B}H[0])$. Apply the exact derived functor $S_x$ from Step 2. The complex-level stalk tensor isomorphism identifies its representative with $Q\operatorname{Tot}(S_xP\otimes_T S_xH[0])$. Here scalar transport across $e_x$ commutes with tensor: the map on pure tensors is $p\otimes h\mapsto p\otimes h$; the balancing relation by $a\in T$ is the relation by $e_x(a)\in B$, and bijectivity of $e_x$ gives the inverse. The differential is $d_P\otimes1$ because $H$ is in degree zero. By Step 3 and the module K-flat tensor-model theorem, this object is isomorphic to $Q(S_xP)\otimes_T^{\mathbf L}S_xH$. Finally apply the derived tensor bifunctor to the isomorphisms $\theta_x Q(S_xu):Q(S_xP)\cong Q(M_{\mathfrak q})$ and $\gamma_{\mathcal G}:S_xH\cong\mathcal G_y$ from Steps 2 and 4. This gives exactly the displayed derived-category comparison. All objects and maps here are in $D(T)$, before applying any cohomology functor.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding construction; cohomology.tex Tag 06YB, tensor-stalk identification; derived.tex Tag 015F.

proof.text: Given any $T$-module $L$, regard it as an $\mathcal O_{V,y}$-module via $j^{-1}$ and set $\mathcal G=i_{y,*}L$. In the ringed-module skyscraper definition every neighborhood of $y$ has sections $L$, with identity restrictions between such neighborhoods. The map $\mathcal G_y\to L$ sending a germ represented by $l$ to $l$ is consequently a bijection, with inverse sending $l$ to its germ on $V$. It is linear because a section of $\mathcal O_V$ acts by its germ at $y$. Combining it with the $T$-linear inverse-image comparison of Step 4 yields $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x\cong L$ under $e_x$. Substitution into Step 5 gives the required tensor with $L$. The point $y$ need not be closed: only neighborhoods containing that same point enter this stalk calculation.
